clue.text: Spot scoundrel breaking into safe

indicators.note: something breaking into another word sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to spot is to see
a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain cracks open a strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' sends the scoundrel inside the word for spot. 'safe' looks like the strongbox being robbed, but here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something protected from harm or danger.

clue.text: Breaks stolen picture

parts.note: breaks, as a twig does, means snaps
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in and makes off with a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' and 'stolen' read like a burglary, but they are just two synonyms placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick casual photograph is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Finding accountant exciting Is drinking freely!

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
rousing means stirring or exciting

explanation.surface: Discovering that a stirring accountant goes on a bender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding' and 'Is' are link words joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousing is noisy, merry drinking in company.

clue.text: See 27 down
Pudding Ingredient is a lemon mixture

indicators.note: a mixture of these words means their letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe note saying lemon is part of a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges the letters of IS A LEMON.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse durum wheat grains used to make milk puddings.

clue.text: Sees poor nurse caught accepting perfumes

indicators.note: one piece accepting another takes it inside itself
poor suggests the word is in a bad state, so its letters get rearranged

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone notices a weak nurse being arrested while carrying scents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns SEES into ESES; 'accepting' puts SEN and C in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Essences are concentrated scented extracts, used as fragrances.

clue.text: Order "run round marquee", being all-powerful

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
to nip is to run quickly, as in nip to the shops
O is round in shape
a marquee is a large tent

explanation.surface: A command to dash about a big tent at a fete.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'run round marquee' reads as one instruction, but each of its three words is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipotent means having unlimited power; the definition 'being all-powerful' is an adjective phrase.

clue.text: Bury famous playwright topless!

indicators.note: topless means the first letter, at the top of this down answer, is removed

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a famous British playwright

explanation.surface: A call to lay a naked dramatist to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes the P off PINTER. 'Bury' could be the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave.

clue.text: Scrape off tar on a red woolly

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, AB being an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: woolly means muddled, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Advice to rub something off a fluffy red jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' rearranges A RED into RADE, and 'on' puts AB above it. The page prints 'car', a misreading of 'tar'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away by rubbing or scraping.

clue.text: Monster water outlet no conservationists wanted

indicators.note: no ... wanted says these letters are not wanted, so they are removed

parts.note: a hydrant is a street outlet for water
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage and conservation charity

explanation.surface: Campaigners object to a fire hydrant being installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' (with 'wanted') removes NT from HYDRANT. The many-headed serpent of Greek myth is the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra is the many-headed serpent Hercules fought in Greek legend.

clue.text: A woman soldiers imprisoned before

indicators.note: something imprisoned is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: lady means woman
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A woman held captive by troops in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' locks the soldiers inside the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time, earlier than expected.

clue.text: Seen pointlessly returning duty list to statesman

indicators.note: a point of the compass such as E is lost, so a letter is dropped
returning means this word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: Someone handing an aimless rota to a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' drops E (East) from SEEN to give SEN; 'returning' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elder statesman of government.

clue.text: Fastened pole to shed

parts.note: S is the south pole
a hut is a shed

explanation.surface: Someone nailing a post to a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole' looks like a wooden post, but it is the South Pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is closed and secured has been fastened.

clue.text: Came to light as print changed colour

indicators.note: changed means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: Something emerged when the printing ink altered its hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges AS PRINT into TRANSPI, followed by RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpired means became known, emerged as a fact.

clue.text: Buzz with detail I raised when mortified

parts.note: a buzz is a hum

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means the words are read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: Embarrassment at a buzzing noise when a small point is brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns DETAIL I upward into ILIATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Humiliated means deeply embarrassed and ashamed, as is mortified.

clue.text: Offensive party rejected promissory notes

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so this word is reversed

parts.note: a do is a party
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A political party spurns distasteful IOUs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DO into OD. 'party' looks political, but it is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means repulsive, causing offence.

clue.text: Convinced some

definitions.meaning: as in 'a particular one', like 'a ___ person'

explanation.definitionFit: Means both sure of something and particular but unnamed, as in 'a ___ person'.

clue.text: Basil and Eric, terribly hot-tempered

indicators.note: terribly means badly done, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two men, Basil and Eric, with fiery tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges BASIL and ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Irascible describes someone easily angered.

clue.text: Oriental man gets drunk in secret

indicators.note: one piece in another means it goes inside it

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
Eric is a man's name
a sot is a drunk

explanation.surface: An Eastern man gets inebriated in private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the drunk inside the Oriental man; 'gets' is a link. 'drunk' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means known only to a select few, arcane.

clue.text: Wild boar not supposed to be tree-dwelling

indicators.note: wild means untamed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: something real is actual, not merely supposed

explanation.surface: A wild pig claimed to live in trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges BOAR into ARBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal describes animals that live in trees.

clue.text: Back street opposite

parts.note: back, as in return, means again

explanation.surface: A back street across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back street' reads as one phrase, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Against means in opposition to, set facing.

clue.text: One-sided fun arranging tune

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters in a new order

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A biased musician arranging a light tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' rearranges FUN into UNF, followed by AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means biased, favouring one side.

clue.text: One is spotted suffering from it

definitions.text: One is spotted suffering from it

parts.words: One is spotted suffering from it
parts.note: the clue reads like spotting a culprit, but it describes a skin condition that leaves the sufferer covered in spots

explanation.definitionFit: An itchy skin inflammation that leaves a patchy, blotched rash.

clue.text: Colour of a companion after exercises

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come after the first one

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A friend's hue after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts 'a companion' behind the exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft pinkish-orange shade named after the fruit.

clue.text: Stirring up riot cheer a Roman driver?

indicators.note: stirring up mixes things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rousing cheer at the races in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring up' rearranges RIOT CHEER A. The question mark shows the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drove the racing carts in the Roman circus.

clue.text: One last word before you go

definitions.text: One last word before you go

parts.words: One last word before you go
parts.note: reads as a request for a final remark, but it describes the farewell said when parting

explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived farewell, said on taking leave of someone.

clue.text: Imitate some female choirs

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Women's choirs copying one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'femalE CHOirs'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat or copy, as a sound bounces back.

clue.text: And down Mistake route which gets you on to motorway

definitions.text: which gets you on to motorway

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake
a road is a route

explanation.surface: An error in the road that leads onto the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And down' is the remains of the cross-reference '27 and 3 down' in the printed text. A slip road is a British term for a motorway on-ramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A short road joining a motorway, the British name for an on-ramp.

clue.text: He turns out to be first easy winner

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A man proves to be the first to win easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He turns out' looks like 'he proves', but it means one who turns people out of their home.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is someone who expels tenants from a property.

clue.text: Worry about politician becoming bore

indicators.note: one word about another surrounds it

parts.note: care is worry
LIB is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: Anxiety that a politician is turning dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the worry around the politician. 'bore' looks like a dull person, but it is a gun barrel's width.
explanation.definitionFit: The calibre of a gun is the internal diameter of its barrel.

clue.text: One carries some water over

parts.note: reads like someone fetching water, but it describes a bridge structure that channels a waterway across a valley

explanation.definitionFit: A bridge-like structure built to convey a channel across a valley.

clue.text: Beg for a stewed apple

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Pleading to be given some stewed fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed' rearranges A APPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to plead or ask earnestly.
